paper.citation: Syed, Rager & Conmy 2024, 'Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery', arXiv:2310.10348 (NeurIPS 2023 ATTRIB Workshop / BlackBoxNLP)
paper.eq2_attribution_score: L(x_clean | do(E=e_corr)) ~= L(x_clean) + (e_corr - e_clean)^T . dL/de_clean ;  Delta_e L := (e_corr - e_clean)^T . dL/de_clean
paper.eq3_absolute_attribution_score: |Delta_e L|  (paper always ranks by the absolute attribution score, averaged over (x_clean,x_corr) pairs)
paper.sign_note: Paper writes (e_corr - e_clean); the reference repo writes (clean - corr). These differ only in sign; both are taken |.| when ranking (Eq 3 / attr_absolute_val=True). BLME uses (clean - corr) then abs -> matches the repo convention and Eq (3) exactly (sign-invariant).

anchors.first_order_approx: EAP is a first-order (Taylor) approximation of activation patching; on a LINEAR model patching is exact -> EAP score == true patching effect (Part B: d=0..1e-16).
anchors.ranking: the edge with the largest |activation-difference x gradient| ranks highest; identical ranking between reference and independent recomputation on gpt2 (Part C).

verdict.full_circuit_pipeline: PROXY — BLME's registered task 'causality_edge_attribution' does NOT run the transformer_lens edge graph; it applies the same EAP KERNEL to residual-stream LAYER inputs (documented in the task docstring). The KERNEL is at numeric parity; the CIRCUIT-level pipeline is a faithful proxy, not the full EAP edge graph.

caveats: BLME is a per-LAYER residual-stream proxy, not the per-EDGE transformer_lens computational graph of the official EAP repo. The task docstring states this explicitly.

BLME downcasts activations/grads to float32 numpy before the kernel (task lines 155-156,168), so BLME-vs-reference at the same formula is exact (0.0) but BLME-float32-vs-reference-native is bounded ~1e-6.

EAP is a FIRST-ORDER approximation of activation patching; it is exact only for models linear in the edge activation (Part B). For real nonlinear transformers it is an approximation (as the paper states).

BLME corrupts by token-shuffling a single prompt rather than using a curated counterfactual (x_clean,x_corr) pair; the paper averages the score over such pairs. This affects the INPUT distribution, not the kernel formula verified here.
Reference architecture is transformer_lens HookedTransformer; BLME uses architecture-agnostic HF forward hooks. The kernel formula is identical; the graph abstraction differs.
